tob-10047: The only complete novel to survive from ancient Rome, Apuleius’s story follows Lucius, a young man turned into a donkey by a witch’s botched magic spell. His adventures as a beast of burden lead him through a comic, often raunchy series of misadventures until the goddess Isis restores him. This is William Adlington’s 1566 translation, the earliest English version.
tob-4047: William Blake’s paired poems show the same world through two lenses — the child’s wonder of Innocence and the adult’s hard-won knowledge of Experience. The lamb and the tyger, the chimney sweeper seen twice over, make this the most loved short book of English verse. Blake printed it himself, with his own hand-tinted pictures.
tob-4185-78147: Book two of Goodwin’s Plutarch carries on the Moralia — on fearful gods, on banishment, on the still life, and more. Plutarch’s blend of tale and counsel made him the old world’s best-loved moral teacher. Each piece is a small masterwork of workaday wisdom.
tob-4147: S. V. Subrahmanyam’s 1911 Garuda Purana turns this great Vishnu-book’s word on death, the afterworld, and burial rites. Its bright tours of heavens and hells shaped Hindu folk-belief for ages. Leeches of souls still read it at death-beds. The volume opened the Puranas to English readers.
tob-10347: Collin de Plancy’s Dictionnaire Infernal — 1818 — is the great French dictionary of demons, famous for its engraved portraits of hell’s court. His compendium lists their ranks, powers, and histories with mock-serious learning. The book remains the classic devil-lore handbook.
tob-10547: Nikola Tesla’s My Inventions is the wizard’s own life story — his boyhood in Croatia, his strange visions, and the devices that lit up the world. Written for a 1919 electrical magazine, it shows his mind unfiltered. The book is key to knowing the man.
tob-13147: John C. Street’s Hidden Way Over the Threshold is a way-book of soul-growth through hidden practice, penned in the early 1900s. The work bridges God-wisdom and workmanlike wonder. Its teaching drew seekers of the wonder-rebirth. The book stays a strange keepsake of its day.
cia-0000103347: An April 1990 intelligence analysis arguing that airplanes were the weak point of Bolivia's cocaine trade. Without small aircraft to fly drugs out of remote jungle labs, the whole business would stall. The report shows the CIA thinking like a strategist about the drug war: find the one link the traffickers cannot replace, and press there.
cia-0000107447: An April 1948 report on Soviet officials in the Levant — the Eastern Mediterranean lands of the Middle East. Written as Israel was being born and empires were withdrawing, it shows the young CIA already watching Moscow's men in a region that would consume American attention for decades. Early Cold War history, straight from the files.
cia-0000108047: A June 1986 report on the use of prison labor in Arkhangelsk Oblast, the vast northern Russian region of forests and ports. Inmates worked the timber industry and other heavy labor in brutal Arctic conditions. The entry extends the CIA's camp map to the far north, where geography itself was part of the punishment.
cia-0000112347: Tale 1 of 2 — an April 1992 report, its title garbled in the archive, on a legal official discussing defense and security issues. The mangled title hides the substance, but the form is familiar: translated foreign press, numbered in sequence. Even imperfect records preserve the habit of watching.
cia-0000117847: The Current Intelligence Bulletin of March 6, 1960 — the CIA's daily roundup of world events for senior officials. Each morning edition compressed the planet's crises into essential reading. This surviving issue freezes one day of the Cold War: what mattered, what threatened, and what Washington was told first.
cia-0000119747: Hungary as of midnight on November 4, 1956 — the very night Soviet forces launched their full invasion of Budapest. The timestamp marks the hour the hope died. This document is history at its rawest: a revolution being crushed, reported as it happened.
cia-0000124247: A February 1960 scientific intelligence monograph — number four in the series — on Soviet space vehicles. By 1960 the space race was a full contest, and every Soviet rocket was catalogued. The document shows the technical deep-dive behind the headlines — thrust, payload, and purpose.
cia-0000132247: Situation Report 564: Saddam responding to something — the truncated title cuts off the provocation. The Iraqi leader's reactions were studied like seismograph readings. The entry is Baghdad's echo, captured: defiance, as always, but the tone was shifting.
cia-0000132647: A May 1960 report: communists set to dominate a Latin American youth conference in Havana — the truncated title suggests the details. The young were the movement's future, and the party knew it. The document is the conference, captured: the youth, organized.
cia-0000132747: A 1961 study of bloc economic and military support for Castro's regime — the truncated title cuts off the second half. The communist world's aid was keeping the revolution alive. The document is the lifeline, measured: the support, tallied.
cia-0000134247: A 1960 report: an Argentine official suggesting a basis for anti-Cuban action. Buenos Aires was building the legal case against Havana. The document is the brief: the official, arguing.
cia-0000136247: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN requesting harmless smoke grenade and flare bomb drops — the archive's spelling says rquesting, the truncated title cuts off the rest. Theatrics, not destruction. The document is the show: the smoke, dropped — the fear, manufactured.
cia-0000136947: A 1954 cable to the senior representative at LINCOLN on the Voice of Liberty broadcasting — the archive's punctuation adds a stray colon. The liberation station, on air. The document is the voice: the liberty, broadcast.
cia-0000141147: A 1961 cable from JMWAVE on the flight schedule of B-26 number 933 and number 927. The bombers, scheduled. The document is the timetable: the aircraft, tasked.
un-ga-res-1747: United Nations General Assembly Resolution 1747, adopted in 1962. The number and date survive in the catalog; the substance lives in the full text. The resolution is the document: the Assembly, resolved.
un-ga-res-47: UN General Assembly Resolution 47, from 1946. The first session's later acts. The entry is the artifact: the forty-seventh resolution, filed.
un-ga-res-a-69-47: General Assembly Resolution A/69/47, adopted in 2014. One of the session's acts. The designation and year are preserved — nothing added, nothing invented.
un-sc-res-47: Security Council Resolution 47, adopted in April 1948 — the Kashmir resolution, expanding the UN Commission for India and Pakistan and calling for a plebiscite. The Council's blueprint for settling the subcontinent's defining dispute — still cited, still unfulfilled. The resolution is the plan: the plebiscite, promised.
un-sc-res-447: Security Council Resolution 447, adopted in 1979 — aligned. The late-seventies Council deliberated. The designation and year survive; the act lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1547: Security Council Resolution 1547, adopted in 2004 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
un-sc-res-1947: Security Council Resolution 1947, adopted in 2010 — aligned. The Council's business continued. The number and year survive; the decision lives in the text.
cia-0000135747: A 1961 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135747. The exiles' record, held. The entry is the record: the exiles, remembered.
plos-pone-0000047: A 2006 PLOS ONE study: Cdx4 and menin co-regulate Hoxa9 expression in hematopoietic cells. Two proteins jointly control a blood-development gene. The paper is the co-regulation: the gene, jointly run.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d47: Marshal Stalin to President Roosevelt, October 19, 1943 — Document 47. Two days later, another. The message is the follow-up: the marshal, again.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d147: The President to the ambassador in Turkey, Steinhardt, November 20, 1943 — Document 147. A second presidential letter that day. The message is the doubling: the day, busy.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d247: Joint Chiefs of Staff minutes, November 22, 1943 — Document 247. The American planners, minuted. The minutes are the planners': the chiefs, conferring.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d347: The president's special assistant Hopkins to the minister in Egypt — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 347. The insider answered. The cable is the answer: Hopkins, to Kirk.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d447: Combined Chiefs of Staff minutes, December 5, 1943 — Document 447. A third session. The minutes are the third: the planners, tireless.
arxiv-2605-09147: Part-of-speech tagging for medieval Romance languages — Old French, Old Occitan — means wrestling with sparse, messy manuscripts. Matthias Schöffel and Esteban Garces Arias compare traditional taggers against LLMs on the task. The 2026 paper measures whether modern AI beats classical tools on ancient tongues.
arxiv-2605-09247: Restricted Boltzmann machines learn quantum states, and the Z2 Bose-Hubbard chain in the adiabatic hard-core regime is a tough test. Gustavo Alejandro Avalos Valentín and Roman Josué Armenta Rico benchmark the machine on it. The 2026 paper is machine learning meets quantum many-body physics.
arxiv-2605-09447: Steering heat-like equations with controls that move around and multiply the state — mobile, multiplicative — is a delicate business. Lingyang Liu studies the controllability of quasilinear parabolic equations under such controls. The 2026 paper is PDE control theory with moving actuators.
arxiv-2605-09747: Labor markets match workers to jobs through a mysterious matching function. Georgios Angelis and Yann Bramoullé take a unified look into the black box, carefully connecting theory to data. The 2026 paper is labor economics on how hiring actually works in practice.
arxiv-2605-09847: The Shafarevich boundedness conjecture limits how many families of polarized varieties can exist; its geometric version is the focus here. Junchao Shentu tackles the geometric Shafarevich boundedness conjecture for families of polarized varieties. The 2026 paper is algebraic geometry at depth.
arxiv-2605-10047: Loss reweighting for imbalanced learning, rethought as an inverse problem through the lens of neural collapse. Jinping Wang, Zixin Tong, Zhiwu Xie, and Zhiqiang Gao offer the new viewpoint. The 2026 paper is imbalanced learning with a collapse-informed conscience. It reframes reweighting as inversion.
plos-pone-0003447: Bone biologists traced a growth signal's stop command in this 2008 paper. The growth factor FGF halts cartilage cells from dividing, and the team showed it works when the enzyme PP2A strips a phosphate off the p107 protein, locking the cell cycle. Since overactive FGF receptors cause dwarfism disorders, the pathway names a possible intervention point.
plos-pone-0003547: Clinicians linked high ferritin to metabolic trouble in this 2008 study. Patients with elevated blood ferritin but no iron overload showed more insulin resistance and fatty liver, suggesting the iron-storage protein flags metabolic syndrome rather than hemochromatosis. The work reframes a common lab finding as a metabolic warning sign.
plos-pone-0003647: In 2008, three builders made a simpler way to clone DNA. Their one-pot, one-step method cuts and pastes gene pieces in a single tube with high care, and it scales to many samples at once. Unlike older tricks, it leaves no junk sequences behind, giving labs a cleaner fast lane for building DNA.
plos-pone-0003747: In 2008, Yaghmur, Laggner, and Almgren watched soap-like blobs morph with heat. Monoelaidin dispersions in water shifted from simple vesicles to complex cubosomes as temperature changed. The self-assembly map guides designs for drug delivery particles built from these shape-shifting fats.
plos-pone-0003847: A 2008 systems biology study connected a metabolic shortcut to fungal growth. Panagiotou, Andersen, and Grotkjær linked the phosphoketolase pathway to growth in Aspergillus nidulans. The analysis shows how this mold's sugar-routing choices set its pace of life.
plos-pone-0003947: In 2008, Stiefel, Gutkin, and Sejnowski showed a brain chemical retuning neuron timing. Cholinergic modulation reshaped the phase response curves of cortical pyramidal neurons. The retuning reveals how attention-linked chemistry rewires spike timing.
plos-pone-0004047: In 2008, Lee, Han, and Meyer blamed jumping genes for flipping chromosomes. Retrotransposons caused several large inversions between human and chimpanzee lineages. The abundant LINE-1 and Alu mobile elements did the flipping. The work shows mobile DNA reshaping ape genomes on an evolutionary scale.
plos-pone-0004147: In 2009, Wan, Zeng, and Ni read the giant panda's immune archive. Giant panda genomic data traced the birth-and-death history of MHC genes. A 636,503-base stretch revealed the immune complex's long evolution. The new sequence aids panda conservation breeding plans today.
plos-pone-0004247: In 2009, Sagara, Arata, and Taniguchi found a protein greasing brain cell movement. Scapinin, a PP1-binding protein, boosted cell spreading and crawling speed. The brain protein linked phosphatase control to faster crawling. The neat finding maps a new cell migration switch.
plos-pone-0004347: In 2009, Desguerre, Christov, and Mayer sorted a cruel disease's faces. Duchenne muscular dystrophy's many faces were split into subtypes. The long-term French study defined predictive groups. The sorting aids therapy trials greatly. The work tackles a major trial obstacle.
plos-pone-0357447: New lava from a volcano becomes a blank canvas for ocean life. This marine biology paper compares the seafloor communities living on recent lava flows with those on older, historical flows around an oceanic island. Tracking which species settle first and how the community changes over time, the study shows how underwater ecosystems rebuild from scratch after volcanic eruptions.
plos-pone-0358947: When blood tests turn up bacteria, doctors face a dangerous wait: which germ is it, and which drug kills it? This paper presents a faster method to identify pathogens from positive blood cultures and test them against antibiotics in one rapid workflow. Cutting hours off the wait means the right antibiotic reaches the patient sooner — and lives saved in sepsis care.
plos-pone-0358647: Behavioral scientists spend hours tracking animals frame by frame in video — or attach markers that change how the animal behaves. TrackStudio is a software toolkit for markerless tracking: it follows animals or body parts in video automatically, with no markers required. The paper describes the integrated tools, giving researchers a faster and less invasive way to measure movement.
plos-pone-0358847: Sanglifehrin A is a natural compound that binds the protein Cyclophilin A, a target with roles in immunity and infection. This paper runs an all-atom molecular dynamics simulation — a frame-by-frame physics model — of the two locked together. Watching how they flex and grip at atomic scale guides chemists designing better drugs from this scaffold.
plos-pone-0358447: Flu drugs flushed into waterways could breed resistant viruses in the wild. This paper assessed the occurrence of influenza antivirals in aquatic environments and the risk of resistance developing in influenza A viruses there. The risk assessment flags an overlooked path by which drug resistance could escape into nature.
plos-pone-0346447: Tuberculosis still kills — and drug-resistant strains are the nightmare scenario. This paper tracked annual trends in TB detection and rifampicin resistance at a regional referral hospital in Northern Ghana from 2019 to 2024. The six-year trends give health officials a clear read on whether local control efforts are winning or losing ground.
plos-pone-0343647: Diabetes drugs only work if patients actually take them. This study identified factors associated with medication adherence among adult diabetic patients in Bangladesh. The factors map exactly where interventions — reminders, cost relief, education — could keep patients on track with their treatment.
plos-pone-0358347: Controlling a 15-joint bionic hand with gestures is a formidable mapping challenge. This paper built a real-time gesture mapping system for a palm-scale bionic manipulator. The system translates human hand movements into smooth robotic motion, bringing intuitive control closer for prosthetics and robotics.
plos-pone-0358247: Japan’s cancer care is stretched thin — and pharmacists could help share the load. This qualitative study examined factors affecting task shifting from physicians to pharmacists in cancer chemotherapy. The findings map what helps and what hinders handing chemo tasks to pharmacists safely and effectively.
plos-pone-0345347: Qatar’s primary care workforce faces the AI wave — ready or not. This mixed-methods protocol will study AI awareness and educational integration among these health workers. The planned research maps readiness levels before the technology arrives in force, so training can keep pace.
plos-pone-0349947: Wet macular degeneration steals central vision — and injections of aflibercept into the eye fight back. This trial compared two-dose aflibercept 8 mg against three-dose 2 mg loading in treatment-naïve neovascular age-related macular degeneration. The head-to-head test asks whether a stronger dose means fewer jabs for patients.
plos-pone-0355847: Malaria in pregnancy threatens both mother and unborn child. This Ghanaian case-control study evaluated HLA-G and hematobiochemical levels and their association with malaria and miscarriage among pregnant women. The immune markers it identified may one day predict which pregnancies are most at risk.
plos-pone-0356547: The pandemic stole America’s sleep — and social media confessed it nightly. This social sensing study tracked pandemic-era sleeplessness using nighttime social media data across the country. The posts reveal a nation’s insomnia in unprecedented detail, night by restless night.
plos-pone-0356147: Scientists sneak Beatles lyrics into their papers — getting by, indeed, with a little help from their friends. This paper used large language models to detect cultural wordplay in scientific literature, with the Beatles as the test case. The AI finds the hidden jokes and references that human readers glide right past.
plos-pone-0345847: Cervical leukoplakia — white patches with malignant potential — is devilishly hard to diagnose where resources are scarce. This Ghanaian study unveiled the diagnostic challenges and used them to inform low-resource screening strategies. The findings adapt cervical screening to the realities of clinics that must do more with less.
plos-pone-0357247: This entry is a correction notice, not a research finding. It amends the paper on activation of mGlu3 receptors stimulating GDNF production in striatal neurons. Readers seeking the accurate scientific record should consult the corrected version of the original article.
plos-pone-0357047: Leprosy’s disabilities persist long after the infection is cured — and they’re routinely under-measured. This hospital-based Bangladeshi study assessed the disability burden of leprosy. The assessment gives rehabilitation programs the data to serve patients medicine has otherwise forgotten.
plos-pone-0356647: Wound dressings should be blood-compatible, antioxidant, and antibacterial — a tall order for one material. This paper synthesized a methacrylic acid-mediated glucoxylan and evaluated exactly those properties, plus acute oral toxicity. The multifunctional material passed its safety and performance tests.
plos-pone-0355547: The Plains Sucker — a humble fish of Canadian prairies — has a population structure worth knowing. This paper mapped it for Pantosteus jordani in Canada. The genetic and demographic structure informs conservation of a species most Canadians have never heard of.
plos-pone-0356747: Near-alpha titanium alloys owe their strength to microscopic deformation patterns. This paper investigated hetero-deformation induced stress and its dependence on microstructural morphology in such an alloy. The findings guide metallurgists engineering titanium for aerospace and medical implants.
plos-pone-0354247: Cars talking to cars can prevent crashes — if safety messages get through first. PDBFS is a novel active routing protocol for prioritized delivery of safety messages in vehicular ad-hoc networks. The protocol ensures that when milliseconds matter, the warning — not the infotainment — wins the bandwidth.
plos-pone-0352247: Cultivated bananas owe more to their wild relatives than anyone suspected. This paper revealed the unexpected contribution of native Musa wild relatives to banana diversity in Mainland Southeast Asia — going beyond domestication’s simple story. The wild genetic infusion is a lifeline for a crop threatened by disease.
plos-pone-0355947: Adolescent psychiatric patients in Nepal carry heavy burdens of violence exposure. This paper examined that exposure alongside socio-demographic and familial risk factors. The findings expose the violence wounding young minds — and the family circumstances that amplify or buffer the harm.
plos-pone-0356247: Radiation damages the gut’s lining — but hyperbaric oxygen might shield it via immune pathways. This paper studied hyperbaric oxygen treatment and toll-like receptor 5 in radioprotection of epithelial cells. The findings suggest pressurized oxygen could protect cancer patients’ healthy tissues during radiotherapy.
plos-pone-0355047: Fuzzy control systems with mismatched basis functions — a practical headache — need rigorous control theory. This paper developed multi-rate sampled-data control for T-S fuzzy systems with that mismatch. The mathematical advances bring stability guarantees to controllers that must work with imperfect models.
europmc-pmc2829047: Sequencing DNA straight from soil or seawater reveals whole microbial worlds, but the field needed an introduction. This 2010 primer explains metagenomics, the study of genetic material taken directly from the environment. The authors walk readers through the methods and possibilities. The primer opened a fast-growing field to newcomers.
europmc-pmc2872647: Brain support cells can be turned into neurons. This 2010 paper shows how to direct astroglia from the cerebral cortex into subtype-specific working neurons. The authors' recipe converts one brain cell type to another. Their work advanced the dream of repairing brains from within.
europmc-pmc2901947: A deadly brain fungus varies by region, and this 2003 paper types it. The authors do DNA typing of Cryptococcus neoformans samples from IberoAmerica. Their catalog maps the germ's diversity across the region. The work aids tracking of a global killer.
europmc-pmc2916847: A DNA region tied to heavy smoking also touches lung disease. This 2010 meta-analysis finds multiple independent loci at chromosome 15q25.1 affect smoking quantity, and compares the signal with lung cancer and COPD. The authors untangle a busy neighborhood. Their work clarified a famous genetic hotspot.
europmc-pmc3053347: Plants flip from embryo to seedling with Polycomb's help. This 2011 paper shows a gene-silencing complex steers the seedling switch. The authors reveal the control. Their work lights up plant development. The complex locks embryo genes away. Crops may sprout on cue with this knowledge.
europmc-pmc3056147: Parkinson's genes got a mutation update. This 2010 review catalogs harmful changes in five key Parkinson genes. The authors map each gene's damage pattern. Their overview guides genetic testing. Families with early onset benefit most. The catalog steers trial enrollment. The update remains a cited reference.
europmc-pmc3084247: Prostate tumors in bone dodge hormone blockade. This 2011 paper ties short androgen-receptor variants in bone spread to treatment failure. The authors reveal the escape trick. Their work points to new drugs. The variants work without any hormone. New pills target the variants directly.
europmc-pmc6682547: Students report record levels of depression and worry, yet campus counseling lines stretch for weeks. This review puts the digital fix on trial: phone apps and web programs built to lift mood and steady nerves. The verdict is hopeful - well-made online tools truly ease symptoms, opening a second door to care when the first is jammed.
europmc-pmc6743147: Vaccines work less well in the elderly - and aging immune systems are why. This review examines immunosenescence: how the immune response frays with age and what that means for vaccination. Understanding the decline points to vaccines designed for older bodies, not just younger ones.
gao-gaoreports-b-309947: A 2007 GAO ruling on a contract fight from Central Texas College. The school said the agency's training-deal award was unfair; the ruling tests the claim and gives the final say. The call shows GAO's bid court serving classrooms as well as corporations — fair play rules apply to campus bidders too.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-1147: The jobless aid system kept shortchanging the working poor in 2007 — GAO's report shows low-wage and part-time workers drawing benefits at meager rates. The rules were built for a full-time world that was fading. The findings ask whether the safety net still fit the jobs Americans actually worked.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-947: Military kids' hospitals were getting paid more in 2007 — GAO's report finds children's hospitals drew higher TRICARE rates than other hospitals, even after case-mix math. The findings unpack the payment gap. The report asks whether the premium bought better care or just better billing.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-847: Visa demand was outrunning the system in 2007 — GAO's report says border strategy needed a long view to keep pace. The findings warn that the welcome mat was fraying under the crowds. The report's pitch: plan for the lines, or the lines plan for you.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-647: Asking troops to pay more for care was on the table in 2007 — GAO's report says the TRICARE cost-share ideas would trim the health bill, with trade-offs. The findings price the proposals. The report frames the dilemma: sustain the benefit, or sustain the budget.
gao-gaoreports-b-299547: Northwest Heritage Consultants took its May 2007 contract fight to GAO, and this ruling is the verdict. The firm said the agency's award was unfair; the call tests the protest against bid law. Heritage consulting deals get the same fair-play hearing as any federal buy.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-247: The IRS's computer modernization money got a GAO review in 2007, and the report examines the agency's expenditure plan for the year. The findings grade the spending. The report asks whether the tax collector's tech billions were buying progress. The modernization money had to show results.
openalex-w7206208247: Electricity bills matter even to universities. This case study analyzes what happened when the A. C. Simoes campus of the Federal University of Alagoas was forced to switch tariff groups, from A4 Green at 13.8 kV to A3 Blue at 69 kV, under national energy rules. The authors calculate the financial impact of the migration. A concrete look at how regulation translates into real money for a large public institution.
openalex-w7204190147: Minecraft is secretly a math classroom. This study asked participants in a 2022 math-festival workshop what mathematical ideas they spotted while playing the block-building game. The authors analyzed perceptions of statistics concepts hiding in the gameplay. Playful and clever, it shows how a beloved game can smuggle in serious learning.
openalex-w7204216547: In the quilombola community of Helvecia, Bahia, funk music meets ancestral tradition. This article studies how young people blend the global beat with local heritage through the group Os Brutos. The authors show tradition as living and remixing, not frozen. A vivid ethnography of youth culture at the crossroads.
openalex-w7160334247: Inside exotic quantum materials, electric current can flow along the edges in strange ways. This theoretical physics paper studies a duality between two kinds of particle tunneling in fractional quantum Hall states, systems where electrons act collectively. The authors introduce a new mathematical tool, the phase-shift instanton, to handle the calculations. Abstract but precise work at the frontier of quantum theory.
openalex-w7161687547: In spiral-shaped crystals, atomic vibrations can hand twist to electrons. This theoretical paper explains chirality-induced orbital selectivity: how truly chiral phonons, quantized sound waves, pass angular momentum to electron orbits in helical crystals. The authors work out the quantum details. Esoteric but elegant physics of handedness at the atomic scale.
openalex-w7214911347: Liver surgery bleeds heavily, and this study tested a blood-saving trick. The team tried giving 50 liver-surgery patients their own thinned blood back during the operation. They tracked safety and results. A surgery study of wasting less of the patient's own blood.
pmc-13470147: This 2026 systematic review asks what lived experience — mental health professionals' own history of mental illness — brings to their practice. By gathering studies on the topic, the authors assess how personal experience shapes empathy, trust, and treatment. The review speaks to an important conversation about who gets to be an expert in mental health care.
pmc-13464047: A 2026 chemistry paper on bio-inspired capture of rare earth elements — the metals in phones, magnets, and batteries that are hard to mine cleanly. The authors take design cues from biology to build systems that selectively grab these elements from solution. Greener recovery routes could ease both supply crunches and mining damage.
pmc-13459647: This 2026 meta-analysis pools studies to estimate cardiovascular disease risk in women with endometriosis, a painful condition where uterine-like tissue grows outside the uterus. By combining many datasets, the authors give a clearer answer than any single study could. The result matters for long-term care of millions of women.
pmc-13549947: A 2026 computational biology paper introducing trans-dimensional Bayesian model averaging for carbon-13 metabolic flux analysis — inferring the rates of metabolic reactions while accounting for uncertainty about the model structure itself. Evidence-based flux inference under model uncertainty gives more honest answers. The method serves systems biology and metabolic engineering.
pmc-13288447: A 2026 four-society study on strong-tie and weak-tie rationalities — predicting public stigma, support networks, and health behaviors during COVID-19. Close bonds and loose acquaintances shaped pandemic behavior differently. The cross-society comparison is the study's scope.
pmc-13273447: A 2026 neuroscience paper showing that astrocytic mGluR5 regulation of synaptic transmission is activity-dependent in adult rats. Astrocytes — the brain's support cells — tune synapses based on how active they are. The finding adds nuance to the tripartite synapse.
pmc-13422847: A 2026 feasibility study designing and validating an immersive virtual rehabilitation system for vestibular disorders. VR for balance rehab is promising. The feasibility data support it.
pmc-13523747: In this 2026 physical chemistry paper, water structure within ternary solvents suggested nanophase formation — tiny separated domains in the mixture. The nanoscale organization affects chemistry. The structural evidence is the discovery.
pmc-13529147: In this 2026 case report, a pulmonary embolism with pulmonary infarction following mixed hemorrhoid surgery was treated and analyzed. The post-surgical clot was the complication. The case is the lesson.
pmc-13525547: In this 2026 systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis, positive and negative symptom changes in schizophrenia patients on antipsychotics were analyzed. The dose-response curve is clinically vital. The meta-analysis is the evidence.
pmc-13502747: A 2026 US study of pneumonia mortality trends among adults from 1999 to 2023. The quarter-century trends were charted. The mortality data inform prevention.
pmc-13471647: A 2026 machine learning paper on reliable apparent permeability prediction through benchmarking, stability, uncertainty quantification, and explainable AI. The drug absorption prediction was hardened. The reliability framework is the contribution.
pmc-13454547: A 2026 paper linking accelerated anthropometric ageing to loss of physical function and lower extremity body mass. The body's aging was quantified. The link is the insight.
pmc-13452547: In this 2026 green chemistry paper, efficient solketal synthesis via acetalization used sulfonated carbon from lavender leaf waste after essential oil extraction. The waste became a catalyst. The synthesis is the circular economy.
pmc-13410947: This 2026 commentary, "Reimagining Hepatitis C Elimination: Time for Actions, Not Targets," demanded action over metrics. The elimination agenda was reframed. The commentary is the call.
pmc-13385647: This 2026 scoping review examined artificial nutrition support during acute illness in pregnancy. The evidence on feeding the critically ill pregnant patient was mapped. The review guides a difficult decision.
pmc-13284447: A 2026 7-tesla fMRI paper detecting task-evoked functional activation and coupling with CSF flow in the human brain using ultrashort echo time imaging. The brain-CSF coupling was visualized. The detection is the technical feat.
pmc-13247847: This 2026 study examined structured telehealth community health worker-clinician feedback and diabetes outcomes. The feedback loop improved diabetes care. The structure is the intervention.
pmc-13428147: This 2026 real-world, national, multicenter study examined surufatinib's efficacy in advanced grade 3 neuroendocrine tumors. The drug's real-world performance was measured. The study informs oncology.
pmc-13515147: This 2026 paper showed a novel Ag/AgCl/Ag3PO4 nanocomposite demonstrated potent antibacterial activity against multidrug-resistant and pan-resistant pathogenic isolates (the title is truncated). The silver nanocomposite killed the superbugs. The demonstrating is the antimicrobial advance.
pmc-13472847: This 2026 narrative review examined plant-derived bioactives in depression-related and antidepressant-associated sexual dysfunction. The botanicals' sexual effects were surveyed. The review is the evidence map.
pmc-13466847: A 2026 cross-sectional comparative study of bone turnover markers, DXA, and mineral metabolism in long-term kidney transplant recipients. The transplanted patients' bones were profiled. The comparison informs care.
pmc-13452147: This 2026 review covered circulating tumor DNA in gastrointestinal cancers — promise, pitfalls, and the path forward. The liquid biopsy's GI role was weighed. The review is the balanced outlook.
pmc-13427047: This 2026 knee surgery paper described medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction using gracilis with pes anserinus preservation and adductor magnus pulley. The refined technique was detailed. The describing is the surgical contribution.
pmc-13426447: This 2026 materials paper presented a stimuli-responsive metal-organic polyhedra-based hydrogel membrane for switchable CO2/H2 separations. The smart membrane switched selectivity. The membrane is the separation advance.
pmc-13421347: This 2026 mathematical physics paper presented horizon data — existence results and a near-horizon equation on general null hypersurfaces. The black hole mathematics was formalized. The results are the theoretical contribution.
pmc-13420347: A 2026 retinal paper: SPI1 promoted TNF-alpha-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition-like changes in retinal pigment epithelial cells — implications for age-related macular degeneration pathogenesis (the title is truncated). The transcription factor drove the retinal change. The promoting is the mechanism.
arxiv-2606-16047: When people argue, some claims support others and some attack them — mapping those relations is key to understanding debates. This paper sets up a multi-agent debate system where AI agents argue about argument structure, with "confidence gating" deciding which relations to trust. It converts the components of an argument into a graph of support and attack links.
arxiv-2606-15847: Floer math is a prized engine for counting loop paths in twisty shape-space. This paper lays the base stones of a whole-number take on it — sums over 1, 2, 3… not smooth reals — which nets finer catch. Base-laying math for shape-space pros.
arxiv-2606-16247: Databases pick the order in which to join tables, and a bad order makes queries crawl. This paper improves join-order optimization using hybrid quantum-classical methods for QUBO problems — a mathematical form quantum hardware handles well. It targets database and quantum-computing researchers exploring practical quantum speedups.
arxiv-2606-16547: The 'dark bubble' yarn says our all sits in a blown bubble in a wider deep. This paper weighs light waves that tug themselves — light held by its own heft — inside that yarn. Far-out sky yarn for all-shape dreamers.
arxiv-2606-16647: Line-up math (normal order) files quirk bits in neat rows — a shop-worn aid. This paper widens the old Bell count-rows that bloom from wide line-ups, and charts the new rows' kin laws. For count-row sages and quirk-math fans. Wide rows, wide reach.
arxiv-2606-16847: Diffusion language models write by unmasking text step by step — but they can wander. This paper steers them with a 'latent roadmap': anchor tokens that mark the route, allowing revocable decoding (backing up when wrong). It is for researchers improving diffusion-based text generation.
